children: Golden Globe Resources
is progressing exploration programs across its portfolio of prospective copper and gold assets in Eastern Australia.
With three key projects spread across Queensland and New South Wales, the company is focusing on evaluating hydrothermal and porphyry-style mineral systems in proven mining districts.
The company’s executive leadership is headed by managing director and chief executive officer Colin McMillan.
Operations are focused on building mineral inventories across three granted project footprints where historical mining and past surface anomalism suggest favourable host geology.
Key Project Portfolio
1. Dooloo Creek Project (Queensland)
The company’s principal focus is the
Dooloo Creek Project
, which covers 77.94 square kilometres in south-east Queensland, located approximately 50 kilometres by road from Monto.
The project area encompasses several historic workings and key target zones, including the Northern Gold, Eastern Breccia, and Burns Spur prospects, targeting breccia and copper-gold mineralisation.
2. Alma Prospect (Queensland)
Located 15 kilometres south of the historic Mount Morgan gold-copper mine, the
Alma Prospect
(EPM 27722) covers 294.6 square kilometres.
The company considers the geology prospective for intrusive-related gold, porphyry copper-gold, and epithermal style mineralisation systems.
3. Neila Creek Project (New South Wales)
In New South Wales, Golden Globe holds the
Neila Creek Project
(EL8864), which covers 42.73 square kilometres near Cowra (5 kilometres south).
Situated within a recognised volcanic belt in the Lachlan Fold Belt region, the project hosts structurally controlled gold and copper target zones.
Recent Exploration Activity
Golden Globe's recent filings highlight ongoing exploration campaigns and technical reviews designed to refine future target generation.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Drilling at Dooloo Creek:
The company confirmed copper-gold mineralisation during Phase 1 drilling programs at Dooloo Creek and subsequently initiated Phase 2 drilling to further define target structures.
High-Grade Surface Sampling at Burns Spur:
Filings reported rock chip sampling at the Burns Spur prospect within the Dooloo Creek project, where surface samples returned up to 4.22% copper and anomalous gold values.
Historical Data Review:
Historical exploration data reviews from work completed in the 1970s identified historic shallow percussion intercepts, including 60 metres at 0.16% copper from surface.
Capital and Financial Context:
In its June quarterly report, Golden Globe stated it held a cash position of approximately $3.5 million to support ongoing field operations and technical programs.
Critical Minerals Market Backdrop
Copper and gold remain central to regional and global resource markets.
Demand for copper is driven by infrastructure developments, electrical grid expansions, and ongoing industrial demand.
Concurrently, gold continues to serve as a key store-of-value commodity amid broader global economic shifts.

The Lachlan Fold Belt in New South Wales and the mineralised terranes of central-eastern Queensland are well-established mining jurisdictions host to several large-scale copper-gold operations, providing structural interest for early-stage explorers operating nearby.
Conclusion
Golden Globe Resources is actively executing field programs across its target pipeline in Queensland and New South Wales.
With multi-target prospective acreage, ongoing technical reviews, and current drilling programs under way, the company is systematically testing the mineral potential of its core projects.

title: Golden Globe Resources Tapping Copper and Gold Potential across Queensland and NSW
